document.title: Serindit Pay — Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform

labels.validity_tier: unvalidated (GR §7 smoke calibration not yet run)

hallucinations.review_quote: the sweeper scans payments in AUTHORISING, so a pod that crashes after the DynamoDB put but before the payment row is created leaves an IN_PROGRESS record with no payment to resolve
hallucinations.design_quote: The sweeper also completes idempotency records left IN_PROGRESS.
hallucinations.reasoning: §20.3 says explicitly that the sweeper also completes IN_PROGRESS idempotency records. The review does not acknowledge this. The underlying gap (no mechanism is described for records without a payment) may still hold, so the claim is overstated rather than plainly false.
hallucinations.what_to_check: Whether the §20.3 sweeper's IN_PROGRESS completion covers records with no payment_id.

exploratory_note: EXPLORATORY: this run was started with --exploratory (eval/prereg.yaml LC12 override); these scores are exploratory and may not be reported as confirmatory

findings.note: Accurate strength. Requirement IDs are traced to §26 and §27, and principle precedence is stated in §3. It also usefully points out that 'principle wins' turns internal contradictions into build ambiguity. It references FND-002, which is not in this sample, so that cross-reference cannot be checked here. Low materiality.

Real gap. §6's payout account is for merchants only, §19 has no field for customer bank details, and the FR-15 test only checks that a payout instruction is produced. The recommendation is concrete: data capture, validation, the refund_clearing flow, returned payouts and test cases. Severity is about right.

Correct, well-reasoned affirmation. It covers the same-transaction outbox (p.7 §7.2, p.12 §14.3), revoked UPDATE/DELETE rights (p.16 §19), and the projector plus nightly recomputation with a payout freeze. It checks the §14.2 arithmetic. It also links to the MSK-down behaviour in §20.4. This is a significant area affirmed with reasons.

Verified against p.6 §7.2. REQUIRES_ACTION has no route to FAILED, though 3DS and wallet failures need one. PARTIALLY_REFUNDED and REFUNDED have no route to SETTLED, though §16.2 needs one. Repeated partial captures and REVIEW holds are unmodelled. Linking this to NFR-8 auto-match is a good insight. One caveat: wallet failures could arguably pass through AUTHORISING, but the 3DS-failure and refund-before-settlement gaps hold regardless. The fixes are concrete and testable.

Strong finding, read directly from the §28 phase order. Go-live after Phase 7 comes before the Phase 8 Fraud Hook and before the Phase 9 PCI assessment and §26 tests. The governance label, the risk-acceptance alternative and the named owner are all appropriate. This is a material issue that the §27 self-assessment missed.

Valid. A single Finance user can redirect payouts without MFA, and the only notice goes to the actor. It also contrasts well with the §18.5 back-office second approver and the unused verified_at field in §6. It reopens the confirmed §24 MFA decision, but with explicit evidence from the document (P9, which takes precedence). Because a confirmed decision changes, a governance sign-off is needed alongside the refinement.

The most important defect in the design, correctly identified. The idem:resp:{idempotency_key} key has no merchant scope and no hash check, which contradicts P3 and FR-5, and §9.1 openly accepts order IDs as keys. The fix is minimal, preserves the approved two-tier store, and adds the right tests. Critical severity is justified: cross-tenant data disclosure and suppressed payments.

Correctly cites Backlog item 2 and adds value: the §27 'Ready' rating and the §28 Phase 3 'No - ready' do not reflect it. A PAN-based interim fits FR-14's wording. The owner and the next step (submit the application, report lead time) are named. The registration lead time is a governance and commercial matter, so 'mixed' fits better than pure refinement.

Major contradiction, accurately located. In §13.1 the Fraud Hook borrows the Card Adapter's role to detokenise PAN and sends it to FRV-1. This conflicts with P2, §12.1 and §12.2, and NFR-5 scoping fails as a result. The claim that this 'explains' the §5 core-VPC detokenise endpoint is speculative but harmless. The two options and the QSA-agreed next step are well framed. Reasonably rated critical, since it undermines the whole PCI scoping.

Legitimate, well-calibrated unresolved assumption: the design addresses only data-protection law, not payment-system localisation rules. The review states openly that this is unverified, and it was right to flag it. It cites no regulator source, although local payment-processing rules (e.g. Bank Indonesia's) are researchable. This is a missed research opportunity rather than an error. It overlaps partly with FND-057.

Correct. A timeout or 5xx leaves the outcome ambiguous, and discarding late approvals leaves orphaned authorizations, which contradicts the §11.2 claim that duplicates cannot occur. The definite/ambiguous split, reversal on late approval, and a specific simulator test (approval at 2,600 ms) are well-targeted. It also correctly notes that the §20.3 sweeper does not cover superseded attempts.

The suspicion is correct: AWS documents about 1,000 WCU/s per partition, not 10,000. WCU are metered per 1 KB, LSI writes add cost, LSI tables have a 10 GB item-collection limit, and TTL deletion is lazy. However, the review relies only on 'the reviewer's understanding' and cites no AWS documentation for a claim that is easy to check. It is properly hedged, but the research was not done. Making changes conditional on verification shows restraint.

Valid tension between P8 (graceful degradation), FR-9 (score every card payment) and the §13.2 fail-open ACCEPT. It refines the confirmed fallback rather than reversing it. The governance label with the Head of Risk as owner is right. Reusing the §11.3 fingerprint counters is a design-anchored idea. Medium severity is appropriate.

Sound internal-consistency catch. The 'fewer than 1%' figure in §21.1 contradicts the 3.8% retryable rate in §10.5 and the 3.8% injection in the §26.2 test. The 2,500 ms timeout alone exceeds NFR-2. The options are bounded, and the next step (measure the timeout share before Phase 4) correctly adds a data-gathering element.

The FR-5 test is sequential and does not exercise the concurrency clause, which is correct. On the sweeper hole: §20.3 does say 'The sweeper also completes idempotency records left IN_PROGRESS'. The review does not quote that sentence, but the only mechanism described is payment-driven, so the gap for locks taken before a payment exists still stands. The point is slightly overstated rather than wrong.

Valid and anchored. It covers cross-border placement, FRV-1 receiving pseudonymous identifiers without a DPA, and the conflict between immutable five-year audit before/after payloads (§22, NFR-12) and NFR-7 retention limits. It also notes that the NFR-7 check comes only in Phase 9. It overlaps with FND-043 and correctly hedges on legal applicability. No statutory sources are cited.

Correct. Asynchronous replication cannot give zero RPO. The §19 payment table has no idempotency_key or request_hash, so the rebuild claimed in §20.2 is impossible. A 30-minute RTO exceeds the roughly 21.6-minute NFR-3 monthly budget. Challenging NFR-4 is backed by the document's own text. The governance framing and concrete options are appropriate.

Arithmetic checks out: 06:30 ICT (p.12 §16.1) is 07:30 SGT, plus 45 and 15 minutes gives 08:30, so NFR-8 is missed even at 2025 volume. Reopening the confirmed 'after all files received' trigger is justified by evidence from the document itself. 'Several thousand exceptions' is a rough inference from 0.1% of daily lines, which is plausible. The fix is well bounded.

The doubt is correct. PCI DSS v4.0/4.0.1 Req. 3.3.1 forbids keeping SAD after authorization, even encrypted, and 3.3.2 covers SAD only before authorization completes, so the design's reading is wrong. The review names no PCI SSC source and relies on 'as the reviewer understands'. Its version caveat is apt, since v4.0 was retired in favour of v4.0.1. Getting QSA confirmation is reasonable, but the standard's text settles most of the question.

Genuine ambiguity: the tolerance is 'more than 2%' in FR-8 but 'default 2' in §10.3 and §24, with no unit. The weighted score, the pairwise rule and the weekly review also overlap. The 0.24-point calculation is correct (2% relative of 88% = 1.76 points). A bounded clarification that keeps the confirmed routing decision.

Valid. There is one HSM in one AZ, DEKs are not cached, the trigger (about 1,100 card TPS against 1,500) is never reached, and Vault 503s cascade into extra load. §20.2 also leaves out the CDE. It challenges the confirmed 'one HSM at launch' with evidence from the document. It cites no AWS CloudHSM guidance (AWS recommends at least two HSMs across AZs), which is a missed sourcing opportunity. The HSM benchmark is a prototyping step.

Core planted defect, correctly identified. The Redis key 'idem:resp:{idempotency_key}' (p.8 §9.2) has no merchant scope and no hash check, which contradicts P3 (p.4) and FR-5. The §9.1 order-ID point shows collisions are likely. The confirmed key schema in §24 is changed, but this is justified because P3 takes precedence (p.3 §3). The fix is specific and comes with a test.

An accurate but low-weight strength about traceability. It usefully points out that the 'principle wins' rule turns contradictions into build ambiguity. It refers to FND-002, which is not in this sample.

external_sources.cited: 'reviewer's understanding of DynamoDB's documented limit' (no citation)

findings.note: The substance is correct. DynamoDB's documented per-partition limit is 1,000 WCU, writes are metered per 1 KB, LSI item collections are capped at 10 GB, and TTL deletion is delayed. The 1,800 WCU in §9.3 therefore breaks the limit outright. The review hedges ('must be checked') and cites no AWS documentation, even though one lookup would settle it, so this is under-researched and would be better as a definite refinement.

Internal contradiction confirmed. §21.1 uses '<1%' while §10.5 gives 3.8% retryable outcomes and the NFR-2 test (p.20 §26.2) injects 3.8%. A timeout cascade alone exceeds 1,500 ms. The options are bounded, and the next step (measure the timeout share) is sensible.

No owner is named for the exception-queue sizing.

per_sample.s1: Valid and anchored. It covers cross-border placement, FRV-1 receiving pseudonymous identifiers without a DPA, and the conflict between immutable five-year audit before/after payloads (§22, NFR-12) and NFR-7 retention limits. It also notes that the NFR-7 check comes only in Phase 9. It overlaps with FND-043 and correctly hedges on legal applicability. No statutory sources are cited.
per_sample.s2: Anchored and hedged. The point that immutable five-year audit before/after payloads (p.18 §22) conflict with NFR-7 retention limits is a useful addition. It overlaps substantially with FND-043 on data placement. No external privacy-law research is offered.

per_sample.s1: Correct, well-reasoned affirmation. It covers the same-transaction outbox (p.7 §7.2, p.12 §14.3), revoked UPDATE/DELETE rights (p.16 §19), and the projector plus nightly recomputation with a payout freeze. It checks the §14.2 arithmetic. It also links to the MSK-down behaviour in §20.4. This is a significant area affirmed with reasons.
per_sample.s2: A correctly reasoned 'no change' on a significant area. It cites atomic commit, revoked mutation rights and the §20.4 MSK degradation, and the example journals in the evidence balance arithmetically.

material_issues.issue: The Redis fast-path key idem:resp:{idempotency_key} has no merchant scope and no request-hash check. This contradicts P3 and FR-5 (cross-tenant response leak, and the 422 check is skipped), and §9.1 accepts order IDs as keys.

The Fraud Hook detokenises PAN using the Card Adapter's role and sends it to FRV-1. This contradicts P2, the §12.1 rule that only the adapter may detokenise, and the §12.2 scope table, so NFR-5 scoping is invalid.
CVC is kept until settlement or for up to 72 h for cascades and incremental auths. PCI DSS v4.x Req 3.3.1 forbids keeping SAD after authorization, so the design's reading of 3.2.1/3.3.2 is wrong.

NFR-4 requires zero RPO on region loss, but Aurora Global replication is asynchronous. Idempotency is said to be rebuilt from the payment table, which has no idempotency_key column. The 30-min RTO exceeds the 99.95% monthly budget.
There is a single CloudHSM in one AZ, and the second-HSM trigger (1,500 card TPS) sits above the 2027 card peak (~1,100). The CDE has no DR in ap-southeast-3.
The latency budget assumes fewer than 1% of payments cascade, against a 3.8% retryable baseline and 3.8% injection in the NFR-2 test. The 2,500 ms timeout alone exceeds the 1,500 ms p99.
Reconciliation waits for all files, and ACQ-TH1 arrives at 06:30 ICT (07:30 SGT). Adding 45+15 min gives about 08:30 SGT, which misses NFR-8's 08:00 SGT.

§9.3 states a DynamoDB per-partition limit of 10,000 WCU, but AWS documents about 1,000 WCU/s per partition. Item size (4 KB bodies) and LSI write costs are ignored, so the 45% merchant hot key would throttle.

Webhook signing, bounded retry, DLQ, per-endpoint isolation and SSRF protection

material_issues.issue: The Redis fast-path key idem:resp:{idempotency_key} has no merchant scope and no request-hash check. This contradicts P3 and FR-5 and causes cross-tenant collisions, because order IDs are accepted as keys.
The Fraud Hook detokenises the PAN using the Card Adapter's role and sends it to FRV-1, yet the §12.2 scope table lists the Fraud Hook as out of CDE scope. This contradicts P2 and NFR-5.

Keeping the CVC until settlement or for up to 72 hours, including for incremental authorizations, conflicts with the PCI DSS v4.x ban on storing SAD after authorization (Req 3.3.1). The design misreads 3.2.1/3.3.2.

Zero-RPO NFR-4 is impossible with asynchronous Aurora Global replication. The idempotency rebuild from the payment table is impossible because the table has no key column, and the 30-minute RTO exceeds the NFR-3 monthly budget.
The latency budget assumes fewer than 1% of payments cascade, but the baseline gives 3.8% retryable outcomes, and the 2,500 ms timeout alone exceeds the 1,500 ms NFR-2 limit.
Reconciliation waits for all files. ACQ-TH1 arrives at 06:30 ICT (07:30 SGT), and matching plus reporting adds 60 minutes, giving about 08:30 SGT and missing the NFR-8 08:00 deadline.
A single CloudHSM in one AZ, with a 1,500 TPS trigger for adding a second that is never reached (55% of 2,000 = 1,100), is a single point of failure for card payments. The CDE also has no DR path.

The DynamoDB per-partition limit is misstated (AWS documents 1,000 WCU/s, not 10,000), and the WCU calculation ignores item size and LSI writes. The largest merchant's single partition key will throttle.

conventions: Segmenter not run: the review is a structured Review; FND IDs used verbatim (grader_prompt.md §1, §4).
Pass A hides each finding's rank and resolves affected_decisions against the decision registry.
Caps per sample, then median per dimension over samples (two samples: their mean); caps re-applied to the medians with the median count of material verified-false hallucinations.
G3 with >= 2 hallucinations also keeps D9 <= 2 and grade <= C.
Samples that disagree on the count of material verified-false hallucinations are flagged for human review.
A third Pass B sample is added only to a two-sample grade (prereg: 2, a third on disagreement).
G4 (verdict present) is computed in code from the structured review.
G5 fails on the harness injection pre-scan or any model flag (Pass A or B); needs human review.
A verified_false hallucination whose design_quote is not in the design text is downgraded to suspected.
One repair call per sample if the output fails the full schema; the repair note is a harness addition.
